newsitem.title: USA: Firstar says restructuring improved costs, revs.
newsitem.headline: Firstar says restructuring improved costs, revs.

text.p: Firstar Corp said Thursday its recently completed Firstar Forward restructuring program yielded a $143 million long-term, annualized improvement in its cost structure and revenues.
But the company also said it lost about $33 million in net interest revenue due to a reduction in loans, primarily in Chicago, and distractions caused by the focus on Firstar Forward.
Firstar said loan business has begun to pick up and commercial loan outstandings in the second quarter were up 2.1 percent over the first quarter, or an annualized percentage rate of 8.4 percent.

The $143 million cost and revenue improvement is just above the $140 million goal the company had set for the program, which cut employment at the bank holding company to 7,989 full-time-equivalent positions, from 9,708 in June 1995, when Firstar began planning its restructuring.
The current number includes the addition of 562 positions due to two acquisitions and growth in retail banking, trust, credit card and other businesses.
Aside from the lost loan business, offsetting factors also include $10 million in temporary expenses, Firstar said.

Also, the company anticipates $10 million less income than expected due to a decline in the spread between deposits and loans because of competitive pricing pressure. Finally, the company will reinvest $8 million of the savings each year in additional new technology to maintain and improve its competitive position.
"Clearly, our challenge now is to focus on revenue growth with the same intensity that we brought to Firstar Forward," chief executive officer Roger Fitzsimonds said in a news release.

"In addition to making our financial goal, we have made progress toward our efficiency ratio goal of 55 percent," Fitzsimonds said. "While we will not reach 55 percent for the year 1997, we believe we will reach this goal in 1998, as we continue to emphasize cost control and accelerate revenue growth."
Firstar shares were down 13/16 at 31-1/8 Thursday.
